id="ADR-0002" title="docz is an API package whose first consumer is the CLI" status="Accepted" inferred=false
author="Donald Gifford" created="2026-09-14"
summary="docz is a Go API package. The `docz` CLI is its first consumer, not its product. Every ope…"
context="ADR-0001 (2026-07-03) made `pkg/doczcore/{config,document,docparse,docwrite,toc}` the publ…"
decision="1. **docz is an API package; the CLI is its first consumer.** The API is extracted from wh…"
consequences positive=6 negative=4 neutral=3
alternatives=6 open-questions=5 references=8

positive line=319
  text="**docz is usable as docz from a program.** A consumer calls `repo.Update` or `impl.Parse` instead of copying `cmd/`."

positive line=321
  text="**One design, built once.** The API is specified as a whole and landed as a whole, so the promotion drip ADR-0001 tried to end actually ends."

positive line=323
  text="**The CLI becomes the reference consumer** and the forcing function that keeps logic out of the shell; the swap PR's diff *is* the proof."

positive line=325
  text="**Type packages are additive and isolated.** Adding `pkg/rfc` later is a package that follows R2 and R7, not a redesign; `doczcore` never learns what a phase is."

positive line=328
  text="**Consumers stay in charge of their workflows.** tempy and sdk-booty-sh keep their policy; docz gives them exact lines to act on."

positive line=330
  text="**The CLI is untouched until the swap.** Every landing before it is additive, so `main` behaves as v1.2.2 for CLI users throughout the build."

negative line=338
  text="**A larger frozen surface at v2.0.0.** `repo`, `index`, `doctemplate`, and `wiki` become contract, including shapes ADR-0001 called CLI-flavoured (`index.UpdateOutcome`'s action enum). Mitigated by R4 — enums and reports are typed, wording is not exported — and by the beta window, which lasts until v2.0.0 is cut and in which they may still change."

negative line=344
  text="**Two contracts in the meantime.** Until v2.0.0, the tree carries a frozen tier and an experimental tier and contributors must know which is which (Open Question 1)."

negative line=347
  text="**The swap is one large PR.** Every command's tests must pass byte-for-byte on the new code paths. Mitigated by the existing `cmd/` test suite, which already pins output and exit codes."

negative line=350
  text="**`ParsePlan`'s reversal.** IMPL-0014 dropped a plan model for a stated reason; reversing it needs the reason to be recorded as changed (two consumers, docz's own grammar), not forgotten. Done in Context."

neutral line=358
  text="**No behaviour change for CLI users.** The swap is a relocation; the release notes are for library consumers."

neutral line=360
  text="**Dependencies do not change.** The promoted packages are stdlib + `yaml.v3`, like the core."

neutral line=362
  text="**Release mechanics.** `dont-release` on every PR in this work, the swap included: a `patch` or `minor` label after the module path flips would tag a v1 version on a `/v2` module, which `go get` rejects, and `major` is reserved for v2.0.0 proper. Pre-releases are annotated tags cut by hand (`make release TAG=v2.0.0-beta.N`); goreleaser already marks a suffixed tag as a pre-release (`prerelease: auto`), and `release.yml` gains a tag trigger for them in step 0 so a beta builds binaries (Open Question 3). IMPL-0017's `updated:` field retargets to the v2 line, after this unit."

alternative line=377 label="a" title="Promote on demand, again."
  text="Ship `pkg/impl` and the two `docwrite` byte cores for tempy and stop (DESIGN-0013 Phase A)…"

alternative line=382 label="b" title="Typed models inside `doczcore`"
  text="(`pkg/doczcore/impl`). *Pros:* one import root. *Cons:* every consumer of the core compile…"

alternative line=386 label="c" title="A runtime type system"
  text="(go-cty style, schema-driven types so custom types get models too). *Pros:* uniform. *Cons…"

alternative line=390 label="d" title="Swap `cmd/` incrementally, command by command, releasing as we go."
  text="*Pros:* smaller PRs. *Cons:* the API is designed around what each command needs in isolati…"

alternative line=394 label="e" title="A separate library module."
  text="Rejected in ADR-0001 and again here (Decision 3)."

alternative line=396 label="f" title="This ADR."
  text="API first, layers and rules, one module, standalone type packages with `Doc`, primitives v…"
